sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the advantage of serving G-d through all one's ways is achieved by dedicating mundane activities to Heaven, so that even worldly matters reveal G-dliness.

translations.translation: And likewise is it in the service of man,
that although there is an advantage in the service of "in all your ways know Him"
over the service of Torah and mitzvos,
for through the service of "in all your ways know Him," knowledge of G-dliness is also in worldly matters
("in all your ways"),
nevertheless,
in order that his engagement in matters of permission
("your ways")
be in a manner that worldly matters do not cause him a descent, G-d forbid, and on the contrary, in them themselves he will see Divine Providence
("know Him"),
it is through the service of "all your deeds should be for the sake of Heaven,"
that his intention in engaging in matters of permission is so that through this he can engage in Torah and mitzvos
[and since all his engagement in worldly matters is for the sake of fulfilling Torah and mitzvos, he minimizes them as much as possible and engages in them only to the extent necessary],
and then even when he engages in worldly matters,
he sees in them a revelation of G-dliness,
"know Him."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the precise wording of the Sages that one does not "hold onto" a dispute, meaning the dispute itself is a creation from G-d, and Korach's sin was wanting it to persist, whereas the intent was for Moshe to refine it into a higher peace.

translations.translation: And based on the above, one can also understand the precise wording of the Sages,
"one does not hold onto a dispute,"
specifically "hold onto,"
for the existence of the dispute itself,
that the lower waters were separated from the upper waters,
is a creation created by the Holy One, blessed be He.
And Korach's sin was that he held onto the dispute,
for he wanted the separation to persist
(that the lower waters remain below and not have the thirst to ascend above).
And one may add,
that just as the intent in the creation of the dispute
(the firmament that separates)
on the second day was so that it be clarified on the third day,
when even the separating firmament becomes good,
so too is it regarding the dispute of Korach,
that the intent in this
(as it was from the aspect above)
was so that through this there would be peace in a more elevated manner than before the dispute.
And as explained in the discourses,
that at first Moshe spoke to Korach and his assembly and pursued them with words of peace,
this is,
because Moshe thought that just as the third day
(Tiferes)
clarified the partition and separation made on the second day,
so too would it be regarding Korach,
that Moshe
[who was the third,
Tiferes]
would clarify him.
[But it was not so,
because Korach did not want this,
and his will was to hold onto the dispute].

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Onkelos's translation of "And Korach took" as "And Korach separated" like the separating firmament teaches that even Korach's willful act of dispute was intended from above to be clarified by Moshe.

translations.translation: And based on this, one can explain what the Targum adds, "And Korach took" — "And Korach separated" like the separating firmament,
even though the name of Korach himself hints
(as above)
to the separating firmament
(a firmament like ice),
for the name of Korach
(from the term "baldness,"
whose concept is division)
indicates his nature
(that he was inclined to dispute)
that was created by the Holy One, blessed be He.
But "And Korach took" is the act of dispute that he did by his own will and choice.
And this is what Onkelos the translator innovates, "And Korach took" — "And Korach separated" like the separating firmament,
that even the act of Korach's dispute,
even though this was by his will and choice,
is like the separating firmament that was created by the Holy One, blessed be He.
For just as the intent in the creation of the separating firmament was so that it be clarified on the third day,
so too is "And Korach separated,"
that the intent in this
(from the aspect above)
was so that it be clarified by Moshe,
as above.
